extracted.intended_audience: general readers of classic literature and people who copy/distribute Project Gutenberg eBooks
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for distributing or using a Project Gutenberg eBook (plus incidental commentary on qualities of Hindu/Oriental tales useful to translators, editors, or literary critics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominent license sentence when distributing
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever any copy of a Project Gutenberg work (or any work associated with the phrase 'Project Gutenberg') is accessed, displayed, performed, viewed, copied or distributed, the specific sentence in paragraph 1.E.1 must appear prominently with active links or immediate access to the full Project Gutenberg License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required sentence (starts 'This eBook is for the use of anyone anywhere in the United States and most other parts of the world at no cost...') must appear prominently whenever the work is made available; keep active links or immediate access to the full license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Gutenberg trademark use restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Project Gutenberg' is a registered trademark and may only be used on or associated with an electronic work by people who agree to be bound by the terms of the Full Project Gutenberg License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the Project Gutenberg name/trademark in connection with a work unless you accept the license terms; if you want other terms, obtain written permission from the Project Gutenberg Literary Archive Foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not remove or detach the full Project Gutenberg License
rubrics_metrics.description: You must not unlink, detach, or remove the full Project Gutenberg License terms from this work or any files containing part of this work or any other work associated with Project Gutenberg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the full license attached to any distributed copy unless you have legitimately removed all references to Project Gutenberg (see 1.C) or obtained permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must prominently display the required sentence when redistributing
rubrics_metrics.description: If you redistribute or provide access to a work with the phrase 'Project Gutenberg' associated with it, you must prominently display the sentence set forth in paragraph 1.E.1 with active links or immediate access to the full terms of the Project Gutenberg License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to display the sentence (1.E.1) prominently violates redistribution requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format-conversion requirement and original-format availability
rubrics_metrics.description: You may convert and distribute the work in many formats, but if you provide copies in any format other than the official 'Plain Vanilla ASCII' (or other official form), you must, at no additional cost, provide a copy, means of exporting, or means of obtaining the work in the original official form upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate formats must include the full Project Gutenberg License and must not impose a cost to obtain the original plain form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charging a fee triggers royalty and refund obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: You may charge a reasonable fee for copies/access only if you comply with paragraph 1.E.8 (including paying a 20% royalty of gross profits to the trademark owner and providing refund/return/defect policies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When charging, you must pay royalties (20% of gross profits), provide refunds for users who don't accept the license terms within 30 days, offer replacement or refund for defects reported within 90 days, and comply with all other free-distribution terms unless special permission is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain written permission for other distribution terms
rubrics_metrics.description: If you wish to charge a fee or distribute Project Gutenberg works on different terms than set forth, you must obtain written permission from the Project Gutenberg Literary Archive Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the Foundation as specified in Section 3 to negotiate different terms.

rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a defect is discovered within 90 days, recipients may obtain replacement or refund according to 1.F.3; otherwise the work carries no warranty and the Foundation disclaims liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit of old Hindu tales: suggestiveness and general applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The merit of the old stories 'lies in their suggestiveness and in their general applicability.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In translating, editing, or creating similar tales, favor suggestive details and situations that have wide applicability; these qualities make tales enduring and thought-provoking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tales as didactic amusements (pearls strung as moral lessons)
rubrics_metrics.description: The tales are described as 'a string of fine pearls to be hung round the neck of human intelligence'—amusing narratives that insinuate a lesson in morals or humanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful tale balances entertaining narrative with gentle moral instruction; the moral is often implicit and woven into the amusement rather than preached overtly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milesian/Miletus fables characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Milesian fables are defined as 'gay in matter and graceful in manner' and historically associated with licentious themes; however, this looseness is 'accidental, not necessary.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When emulating Milesian-style tales, aim for lightness and grace; licentiousness is optional rather than essential—purity can be preserved while keeping playful tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hindu tale trait: comparative purity and matrimonial resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Hindu/Indian variants often avoid necessary licentiousness; 'the author almost always takes the trouble to marry his hero and his heroine' and demonstrates 'comparative purity in Hindu literature.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In adapting or translating Hindu tales, expect and preserve tendencies toward moral closure (e.g., marriage) and relative chasteness of content compared to some Western analogues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to readers who enjoy the weird, grotesque, and supernatural
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection 'will especially please those who delight in the weird and supernatural, the grotesque, and the wild life.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize uncanny, grotesque, or supernatural elements when targeting readers who enjoy that mood; maintain wit and an engaging narrative voice to sustain interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storyteller technique: remedy conciseness by 'clothing skeleton with flesh and blood'
rubrics_metrics.description: The translator/editor notes having 'ventured to remedy the conciseness of their language, and to clothe the skeleton with flesh and blood.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For terse source texts, a translator/editor may expand and enliven terse original phrasing to produce readable, engaging English while respecting original meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities/ duties of an ideal king (as narrative model)
rubrics_metrics.description: A king should: replenish his treasury; not oppress when drawing revenues; be informed about his people; punish without partiality; bind enemies safely; be generous; feel equal affection and forbearance towards all. He should preside over justice, be hospitable, observe rites, employ spies and prudent arts in war, avoid favouritism, and administer punishment firmly but justly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting a sovereign in fiction, these traits constitute the classical/Hindu ideal: measured justice, beneficence, self-discipline, ceremonial observance, military prudence, and administrative diligence. The text also gives a detailed daily schedule exemplifying rulerly discipline (waking before dawn, bathing, sacraments, audience, review of troops, limited sleep, etc.) useful for realistic characterization.
